task.name: Secret Scanning Alert Remediation
task.description: Review newly opened GitHub secret-scanning alerts in a covered repository and surface only novel, supported exposures that still require credential invalidation or removal, without retrieving or displaying secret material.
task.intent: Reduce the time that newly detected exposed credentials remain usable and present in repository history while avoiding duplicate remediation requests and preventing secret material from entering workflow outputs.
activationConditions: A GitHub secret-scanning alert is newly opened within the evidence window for a covered repository and identifies a repository location and secret type without requiring access to the detected secret value.
Authoritative alert, repository, and credential-provider evidence supports that credential invalidation, exposed-material removal, or both remain incomplete.
requiredEffects: Each novel remediation finding identifies only the alert number, secret type, affected repository location, required remediation steps, and authoritative evidence references; it never includes the detected secret value.
Maintainers can accept or reject a repository-linked remediation output that calls for both credential revocation or rotation and removal of the exposed material where each action applies.
noopConditions: No newly opened covered secret-scanning alert has supported outstanding remediation work.
Every supported alert is already assigned to an open remediation record, or authoritative evidence shows the credential was invalidated and the exposed material was removed before the run.
successConditions: Each supported novel alert assigned by the run has accepted evidence that the credential was revoked or rotated and that exposed material was removed, or has an explicit supported false-positive resolution, within 72 hours.
Alerts already under remediation and alerts with complete pre-run remediation evidence create no duplicate maintainer attention, and no workflow output contains secret material.
uncertainties: Credential-provider validity or revocation evidence may be unavailable, so repository cleanup alone cannot establish complete remediation.
One credential may appear in several locations or alerts; alert-level deduplication must not imply that credential-level invalidation is complete.
A provider or custom-pattern alert may require maintainer-confirmed false-positive evidence rather than credential invalidation.

operationalValue.statement: The proportion of supported, novel secret-scanning alerts assigned to the run that obtain accepted complete-remediation or supported false-positive evidence within 72 hours.
operationalValue.opportunity: One workflow run and the deduplicated supported novel secret-scanning alerts it assigns in the covered repository.
acceptedEvidence: A repository secret-scanning alert timeline and linked remediation record showing, before the evidence cutoff, both credential revocation or rotation and removal of the exposed material where those actions apply.
An authoritative alert resolution and maintainer-linked record showing the finding is a supported false positive without disclosing the detected secret value.
evidenceRepositories: The repository in which the workflow ran and the secret-scanning alert was opened.

metric.name: verified-remediated-novel-secret-alerts
metric.formula: supported novel secret-scanning alerts with accepted complete-remediation or supported false-positive evidence / supported novel secret-scanning alerts assigned to the run

operationalValue.maturation: 72 hours after the workflow run completes.
operationalValue.zeroRule: Return 0 when at least one supported novel secret-scanning alert was assigned and none has accepted complete-remediation or supported false-positive evidence by the evidence cutoff.
operationalValue.missingRule: Return null when the assigned alert set, repository alert timeline, affected-location state, or required credential-provider invalidation evidence cannot be read without accessing secret material.
